target.title: fix(dashscope): apply request policy to video requests
target.body:
## Summary
- Qwen video generation passes `models.providers.qwen.request` through `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequest` into `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig` before running the shared DashScope video task.
- Alibaba Model Studio video generation does the same for `models.providers.alibaba.request`.
- The shared DashScope video helper now carries the resolved `allowPrivateNetwork` and `dispatcherPolicy` through task polling and generated-video downloads, while preserving the previous fetch/status retry boundary.
- Collision check: searched open PRs for `extensions/qwen/video-generation-provider.ts`, `extensions/alibaba/video-generation-provider.ts`, `DashScope request policy`, `qwen allowPrivateNetwork`, `alibaba allowPrivateNetwork`, and sanitizer references; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## Verification
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qwen/video-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/alibaba/video-generation-provider.test.ts` - passed; 2 shards passed with `Tests  4 passed (4)` and `Tests  6 passed (6)`.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` - passed; exit 0.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/qwen/video-generation-provider.ts extensions/qwen/video-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/alibaba/video-generation-provider.ts extensions/alibaba/video-generation-provider.test.ts src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/provider-http-mocks.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.
- Mutation check A: temporarily removing the Alibaba `request:` argument made `extensions/alibaba/video-generation-provider.test.ts` fail because `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequestMock` was never called.
- Mutation check B: temporarily removing the Qwen `request:` argument made `extensions/qwen/video-generation-provider.test.ts` fail because `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequestMock` was never called.
- Mutation check C: temporarily removing `allowPrivateNetwork`/`dispatcherPolicy` from the shared DashScope poll call made the Alibaba request-policy test fail because the poll `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` options were `{}` instead of carrying `{ ssrfPolicy: { allowPrivateNetwork: true }, dispatcherPolicy }`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Qwen and Alibaba DashScope video generation should honor configured provider request overrides such as custom headers and `allowPrivateNetwork` for submit, poll, and follow-up video fetches.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout using a real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1`, fake literal provider API keys from config, and the exported Qwen/Alibaba video provider runtime paths. No third-party DashScope traffic was sent; Authorization was redacted in output.

Exact command run after this patch:

```text
env HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY= no_proxy= node --import tsx scratchpad/dashscope-request-policy-proof.mts
```

The temporary proof script was not committed. It starts a local DashScope-compatible server, calls `buildQwenVideoGenerationProvider().generateVideo(...)` and `buildAlibabaVideoGenerationProvider().generateVideo(...)` with provider-specific `request.headers` plus `allowPrivateNetwork: true`, and prints the headers the server received.

Evidence after fix:

```text
dashscope-video-request-policy-proof
qwen_videos=1
alibaba_videos=1
submit_routes=qwen-proof,alibaba-proof
poll_routes=qwen-proof,alibaba-proof
auth_headers=Bearer ***,Bearer ***,Bearer ***,Bearer ***
```

Observed result after fix: both providers completed the local DashScope submit -> poll -> download flow, and both submit and poll requests carried the configured per-provider request-policy header.

What was not tested: no live Alibaba DashScope production endpoint was called; the proof validates OpenClaw provider request-policy plumbing locally without sending third-party network traffic.
